details:
It's on the tin. Lumping every interact action into one was a bad idea because of minor differences between interactions.

Before 2024.3.1 HTC Vive controllers used to pose physbones with the grip button click. After 2024.3.1 was rolled out, this is no longer possible without major concessions. One can create a chord to invoke interacts the old way, but this will send *interacts*, not just physbone posing interacts, meaning you'd be able to partially activate trigger and then click grip to activate a udon Interact wrapper. This is goofy.

Worse yet, it isn't possible to mimic the old advanced controller setup: full-pull click would have to remain as is to interact with objects with udon's Interact wrapper. This also means that full-pull on a trigger will pose a physbone, despite having a separate chord set up dedicated to it.

This also introduces unnecessarily extra inconsistencies and extra effort. Originally one could activate any Interact wrappers with a partial pull, but if we choose to stick with full-pull activation, this is no longer the case, you *have* to fully pull the trigger on every activation. Except the UI. UI is fine with partial clicks, for some reason, but only the UI.

This may seem like a rather minor issue, but it isn't, especially if you factor in fine motor control impairments. Sticking with full-pull interaction like this requires extra effort to not activate it now, as well as extra effort to activate every single interactive item. This, naturally, is a significant regression for no particular observable reason.

As such, you should split current "interact" action into three distinct actions:

• interact_udon for interacting with anything interactive like Interact() wrappers

• pose_physbone for posing PhysBone components explicitly

• interact_ui for any UI interactions

This way their thresholds can be explicitly defined, as well as allowing for more complex behaviours to be defined, so the original control scheme can actually be restored.
title: Granularize "interact" action (physbones, UI, Interact())
